text:
Marta (Design): quick heads-up — Export Logs empty state uses "Download logs" but non-admins click and hit a 403. Happens during customer testing.
Andy (Product): oof. we should either change label or intercept click and show a clear next step.
Ellie (A11y): accessibility reminder: whatever we do needs a clear ARIA message and focus management for screen readers. Keep button text concise.
Zane (Eng): simplest: single CTA that opens a modal when user lacks perms. Modal explains restrictions and offers to request access. avoids duplicate UI states.
Marta (Design): two copy ideas for the primary state: 
- "Request export" (for everyone; modal flow if necessary)
- "Download logs" (only for admins) with a hover tooltip "Admins only. Request access."
Which direction?
Andy (Product): favor the modal "Request export" as primary. Tracks intent and reduces surprise 403s. Tooltip ok as supplementary.
Ellie (A11y): modal copy suggestion: header: "Request export access"; body: "Log exports include telemetry and are retained for 30 days. Requesting access notifies your admins and includes the export timeframe." Buttons: "Request access" (primary), "Cancel". Ensure focus trap and announce header.
Zane (Eng): implementation note: when export endpoint returns 403, return a short code in JSON (e.g., `permission_required`) so frontend can surface the modal with prefilled project and timeframe. I'll slot it for next sprint.
Marta (Design): I'll update Figma and the ticket with final phrasing. @design-bot can you add the a11y checklist and link to the spec?
design-bot: checklist added — focus order, aria-live for alerts, labels for buttons, keyboard flow. Spec: https://redwood/specs/export-access-172
Andy (Product): thanks. throwing in a tiny microcopy tweak: use sentence case ("Request export") and avoid the word "logs" in modal header to be less scary for users.
Marta (Design): noted. finalizing now.
